description: The bar chart illustrates the popularity of different large language models—Llama3 (blue), Qwen2 (red), and ChatGPT (yellow)—across three domains: Movies, Songs, and Basketball, with further stratification by answer accuracy (Acc=0 or Acc=1) and ground truth source (GT Ans or Gene Ans), as indicated by the legend. The vertical axis, labeled “Popularity,” ranges from 0 to 220 in increments of 20, representing a quantitative measure of model popularity under each condition. In the “Movies” category, all models show relatively low popularity, with Llama3 (Acc=0 & GT Ans) at approximately 30, Qwen2 (Acc=0 & GT Ans) around 40, and ChatGPT (Acc=1 & GT Ans) near 35. In “Songs,” popularity increases: Llama3 (Acc=0 & GT Ans) reaches ~60, Qwen2 (Acc=0 & GT Ans) ~70, and ChatGPT (Acc=1 & GT Ans) ~75. The “Basketball” category shows the highest popularity across all models: Llama3 (Acc=0 & GT Ans) peaks at ~180, Qwen2 (Acc=0 & GT Ans) at ~210, and ChatGPT (Acc=1 & GT Ans) at ~170. Within each domain, bars are grouped by model and further subdivided by accuracy and answer source, with hatched patterns denoting Acc=0 conditions and solid fills for Acc=1. The chart visually emphasizes that popularity generally increases with domain complexity or specificity (from Movies to Basketball), and that Qwen2 consistently achieves the highest popularity in all domains under Acc=0 & GT Ans conditions, while ChatGPT performs best under Acc=1 & GT Ans in Movies and Songs but trails in Basketball. No explicit sorting of bars by value is applied within each group; instead, the grouping follows the legend order. The chart supports the paper’s exploration of how knowledge popularity influences LLMs’ perception of their knowledge boundaries, suggesting that models exhibit higher popularity (possibly reflecting confidence or output frequency) in domains where they are less accurate (Acc=0), particularly with ground truth answers.
